definitions.explanation: a floor of a building that is below ground level

examples.japanese: {食品|しょくひん}{売|う}り{場|ば}は{地階|ちかい}にあります。
examples.english: The food section is on the basement floor.

examples.japanese: エレベーターで{地階|ちかい}まで{降|お}りてください。
examples.english: Please take the elevator down to the basement floor.

examples.japanese: このデパートの{地階|ちかい}には{有名|ゆうめい}な{洋菓子|ようがし}{店|てん}が{何軒|なんけん}も{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: The basement floor of this department store has several well-known Western confectionery shops.

notes:
Composed of {地|ち} (ground/earth) and {階|かい} (floor/story). Refers to any underground floor of a building. In Japanese department stores, the {地階|ちかい} (often abbreviated as B1) is typically where the food hall ({食品|しょくひん}{売|う}り{場|ば} or デパ{地下|ちか}) is located.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {地階|ちかい}{売|う}り{場|ば}: basement sales floor
- {地階|ちかい}の{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}: basement parking
- {地階|ちかい}に{降|お}りる: to go down to the basement
- {地階|ちかい}{一階|いっかい}: basement level 1 (B1)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {地下|ちか}: underground, basement — more general term, also used as a prefix (e.g., {地下鉄|ちかてつ})
- {地下室|ちかしつ}: basement room — a specific room underground, not a building floor
- {階下|かいか}: downstairs — relative term meaning the floor below, not necessarily underground
